samuel2.3.p1.b1.text: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

samuel2.3.p1.b2.text: And sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;

samuel2.3.p1.b3.text: his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;

samuel2.3.p1.b4.text: These sons were born to David in Hebron.

samuel2.3.p2.b1.text: Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?

samuel2.3.p2.b2.text: Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?

samuel2.3.p2.b3.text: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David …

samuel2.3.p2.b4.text: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.

samuel2.3.p3.b1.text: To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.

samuel2.3.p3.b2.text: Good, … I will make a covenant with you. … Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.

samuel2.3.p3.b3.text: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim.

samuel2.3.p4.b1.text: In the past you sought David as your king. Now take action,

samuel2.3.p4.b2.text: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.

samuel2.3.p4.b3.text: Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.

samuel2.3.p4.b4.text: So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace.

samuel2.3.p5.b1.text: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder.

samuel2.3.p5.b2.text: Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.

samuel2.3.p5.b3.text: What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!

samuel2.3.p5.b4.text: Surely you realize that Abner son of Ner came to deceive you …

samuel2.3.p6.b1.text: … he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David was unaware of it.

samuel2.3.p6.b2.text: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately, …

samuel2.3.p6.b3.text: … and there Joab stabbed him in the stomach. So Abner died on account of the blood of Joab’s brother Asahel.

samuel2.3.p7.b1.text: I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before the LORD concerning the blood of Abner son of Ner.

samuel2.3.p7.b2.text: May it whirl over the heads of Joab and the entire house of his father, …

samuel2.3.p7.b3.text: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.)

samuel2.3.p8.b1.text: Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.

samuel2.3.p8.b2.text: And King David himself walked behind the funeral bier.

samuel2.3.p8.b3.text: … the king wept aloud at Abner’s tomb, and all the people wept.

samuel2.3.p8.b4.text: Should Abner die the death of a fool? Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered.

samuel2.3.p9.b1.text: Then all the people came and urged David to eat something while it was still day, …

samuel2.3.p9.b2.text: May God punish me, and ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!

samuel2.3.p9.b3.text: So on that day all the troops and all Israel were convinced that the king had no part in the murder of Abner son of Ner.

samuel2.3.p10.b1.text: Do you not realize that a great prince has fallen today in Israel?

samuel2.3.p10.b2.text: And I am weak this day, though anointed as king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too fierce for me.

samuel2.3.p10.b3.text: May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil!
